class ActuatorBase

Bases: ComponentBase

Base class for robot actuators.

Mirrors ControllerBase and SensorBase: derives from ComponentBase for common lifecycle (validity, actor, destroy). No concrete actuators exist yet; this establishes the contract early so the first actuator follows the same shape as controllers and sensors.

Registration contract (a RoboticsContext::RegisterActuator<T> template lands with the first concrete actuator, mirroring RegisterController/RegisterSensor): every actuator must declare static constexpr std::string_view TypeName() { return “…”; } (used by the registration templates and for the generated Python type_name() binding), implement std::string_view GetTypeName() const override; // returns TypeName() and provide a uniform constructor ActuatorX(Actor* actor, std::string_view paramArgs, Error& error); that loads its own params from the path or inline JSON. An (Actor*, Params const&, Error&) overload is recommended for programmatic / non-filesystem construction.

Teardown contract (mirrors ControllerBase / SensorBase): get_actor() resolves the live actor on demand and yields None once the owning mochi Scene (or the actor) is gone, so an actuator that outlives its Scene (Scene destroyed before the RoboticsContext) sees get_actor() == None in its destructor. Any concrete actuator whose destructor releases actor-held resources must therefore guard on GetActor() != None (or, for context-owned resources, resolve via GetContext()) so teardown never dereferences a dangling Actor*.

class Bot

Bases: object

Runtime interface to a bot instance in a Scene.

A Bot wraps a single articulated Actor with the controllers, sensors, and actuators created for it. Bots are created via create_bot() and destroyed via destroy_bot(). The RoboticsContext owns the bot memory allocated and deallocated by these functions, respectively. The raw Bot* returned by create_bot() remains valid until destroy_bot() is called or the RoboticsContext is destroyed.

Note

Not thread-safe – like the underlying Scene, a Bot must only be accessed from the thread that owns its scene (usually in an async callback if using async scenes.)

Get the handles of every controller this bot owns.

Covers controllers created through create_controller() and those created on one of this bot’s actors with create_controller() — the owning bot is inferred from the actor (see get_bot_containing_actor()), so how a controller was created makes no difference to whether it appears here. Mirrors get_sensor_handles(): the same set the bot-scoped finders draw from, and the same set destroy_bot() tears down. Resolve each handle with get_controller().

class BotContactOverride

Bases: object

Used to explicitly enable or disable contact between links in a bot. By default, all bots will spawn with contact disabled between links and their first ancestor with a physics body not connected via a Hard joint. This structure can be used to either reenable contact on those pairs, or disable contact between links that are not strictly child-parent. Overrides are applied on bot link actors after spawn using enable_actor_contact_symmetric().

See also

contact_overrides, enable_actor_contact_symmetric()

property enable

Should contact between the pair be enabled?

property link_a

The first link in the pair.

property link_b

The second link in the pair.

class BotJointPrefab

Bases: ArticulatedJointPrefab

Parameters describing a single joint in a bot.

property effort_limit

Maximum effort magnitude that may be applied to actuate this joint [N·m for revolute, N for prismatic]. Interpreted by regime: a negative value (default EFFORT_UNBOUNDED) is unbounded; 0 is non-actuated (no effort can be applied, though the joint still moves freely within its range under external forces); a positive value is a finite limit. This is advisory metadata — it is not copied into the physics articulation, so the sim enforces nothing on its own; controllers may read it (e.g. to clamp their output).

class BotLinearTransmissionPrefab

Bases: BotTransmissionPrefab

Parameters describing a single linear transmission attached to a bot.

Mirrors superdex::experimental::LinearTransmissionParams with an added display name field and SReflect markup so it can live inside BotPrefab and round-trip through the bot’s JSON serialization. The three joint arrays (joint_indices, joint_coefficients, joint_axis_disps) must always be the same length, with one entry per joint the transmission traverses. The remaining fields are inherited from BotTransmissionPrefab which inherits superdex::experimental::DisplacementControlActuatorParams so that one displacement-control actuator can be configured alongside each transmission.

property joint_axis_disps

Displacement along the joint axis [m] for the transmission attachment point at each joint. This allows the transmission to be offset from the joint origin along the axis.

property joint_coefficients

Transmission Jacobian entry at each joint [m / joint-DoF units for a tendon, dimensionless for a gearbox]. Sign encodes direction: positive if the transmission displacement increases with the joint DoF, negative if it decreases.

property joint_indices

Indices into joints identifying which joints the transmission traverses.

class BotSpatialTendonPrefab

Bases: BotTransmissionPrefab

Parameters describing a single spatial tendon attached to a bot.

Mirrors superdex::experimental::SpatialTendonParams with an added display name field and SReflect markup so it can live inside BotPrefab and round-trip through the bot’s JSON serialization. The ordered routing_elements list defines waypoint and linear-joint elements traversed by the tendon. The remaining fields are inherited from BotTransmissionPrefab which inherits superdex::experimental::DisplacementControlActuatorParams so that one displacement-control actuator can be configured alongside each tendon.

property routing_elements

Ordered routing elements defining the tendon path. Must contain at least one element, and every waypoint must be adjacent to another waypoint.

class ComponentBase

Bases: object

Base class for all bots components (controllers, sensors, actuators). Provides common state: the associated actor’s stale-safe identity, a validity flag, and the Destroy pattern. The validity flag is set to false by RoboticsContext before deletion, allowing dangling-pointer detection alongside generational handles.

The associated actor is NOT cached as a raw pointer. Its stale-safe identity (ActorHandle / SceneHandle / owning Mochi context) is retained and get_actor() resolves the live Actor* on demand, yielding None once the owning scene (or the actor) has been destroyed. A component that outlives its mochi Scene (e.g. the Scene was destroyed before the RoboticsContext) therefore never dereferences a dangling Actor* — callers check get_actor() for None. This assumes the mochi Mochi context outlives the RoboticsContext — the outermost lifetime in the mochi ownership graph.

get_actor(self: ComponentBase) → superdex.physics.Actor

Resolve the live Actor* this component is bound to, or None if it was constructed without an actor or its owning scene/actor has since been destroyed. Resolved on demand from the stale-safe handle each call (an O(1) scene lookup), so it is always current and never returns a dangling pointer — dereference only after a None check.

Returns:

Live associated actor, or None if none is available.

get_name(self: ComponentBase) → str

This component’s instance name, or empty if it was created without one. Names are NOT required to be unique, so name-based lookups (FindByName) may return multiple matches.

Returns:

Instance name; empty if unnamed.

get_owning_bot(self: ComponentBase) → Bot

The bot this component was created on, or None if it was created directly on an actor (not via a bot) — e.g. a scene-level sensor or a controller built on a raw articulation. Used to scope FindByName / FindByType to a single bot and to drive DestroyBot’s component cascade. Borrowed: the owning bot is owned by the RoboticsContext, which destroys a bot’s components before the bot itself, so this never dangles. Held as a raw pointer (not a handle) because a bot is not scene-owned, so the stale-safety the actor handles provide is unnecessary here.

Returns:

Owning bot, or None if this component has no owning bot.

get_type_name(self: ComponentBase) → str

This component’s registered type name (e.g. “BASIC_OSC_PD”, “SENSOR_CAMERA”), reported polymorphically. Declared here so controllers, sensors, and actuators can be searched by type uniformly (FindByType); each component kind implements it.

Returns:

Registered component type name.

is_valid(self: ComponentBase) → bool

Whether this component remains usable. Returns false after its owning RoboticsContext destroys it.

Returns:

True while the component is live.

reset(self: ComponentBase) → None

Reset internal state without destroying the component. Parameters are preserved. Use between episodes to clear stale state (e.g., derivative tracking, timing diagnostics).

class ControllerBase

Bases: ComponentBase

Base class for all controllers. Inherits common lifecycle from ComponentBase. Controllers are identified by string names via RoboticsContext registration, not enums.

configure_from_scene_entry(self: ControllerBase, param_args: str, init_args: str) → None

Configure this controller from serialized parameter and initialization arguments. paramArgs is either a params file path or inline JSON; empty uses defaults. initArgs is a controller-specific file path or inline JSON, for example carrying baseLinkName/eeLinkName for link-resolved controllers. Implementations typically deserialize it into a small reflected init-args struct and ignore unrecognized framework keys.

Pure virtual: every controller must implement this uniform configuration entry point. A controller that cannot support serialized configuration should set an error with a clear message rather than silently succeeding.

Parameters:

  • param_args (str) – Params file path or inline JSON; empty uses defaults.

  • init_args (str) – Controller-specific init-argument file path or inline JSON.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

class ControllerBasicOscPd

Bases: ControllerBase

Basic operational-space PD (impedance) controller for robotic arms.

Computes joint torques via the Jacobian transpose method: tau = J^T * F, where F = Kp * pose_error + Kd * velocity_error combines position/rotation tracking errors with PD gains. This is the minimal, robot-agnostic core of operational-space control:

  • No nullspace or posture bias. Redundant (extra-DOF) arms are free to drift in the nullspace; only the end-effector pose is regulated.

  • Per-DOF effort clamping (direction-preserving vector scaling), enabled by default; the per-joint effort limits are harvested from the controller’s BotPrefab (see Initialize).

  • No joint/velocity-limit avoidance, friction/gravity compensation, or inertia decoupling; those belong to richer controllers (see the internal OSC variants).

Intended as a clean, open-sourceable baseline that works on any articulated arm without robot-specific tuning tables.

class RoboticsContext

Bases: object

Resource owner for bots, controllers, sensors, and actuators.

Owns the memory for bots, controllers, sensors, and actuators created through it.

create_actuator(self: RoboticsContext, type_name: str, link_actor: superdex.physics.Actor, name: str = '', param_args: str = '') → ActuatorHandle

Create an actuator of the given type on the given link actor. Unlike a sensor, an actuator always drives a body, so linkActor is required: passing None sets an error and returns an invalid handle. paramArgs is an optional params file path or inline JSON string; empty uses default-constructed parameters. name is the instance name used by find_actuators_by_name() and need not be unique. The owning bot is inferred from linkActor. Returns a handle. For bot-owned actuators, prefer declaring them in the BotPrefab so they are auto-instantiated and destroyed with the bot.

Parameters:

  • type_name (str) – Registered actuator type name.

  • link_actor (Actor) – Actor the actuator drives; must not be None.

  • name (str) – Instance name used by the name-based finders; need not be unique.

  • param_args (str) – Params file path or inline JSON; empty uses defaults.

Returns:

Handle to the created actuator, or an invalid handle on error.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

create_controller(self: RoboticsContext, type_name: str, prefab: BotPrefab, robot: superdex.physics.Actor, name: str = '') → ControllerHandle

Create a controller of the given type for robot. Harvests model-derived configuration (e.g. per-joint effort limits) from the optional borrowed prefab: pass None to create on a raw articulated actor with no model (the prefab must outlive the controller otherwise).

robot may also be None, to drive a real robot with observations pushed in from outside instead of read off a Mochi articulation. Anything that needs the articulation (e.g. reading a Jacobian) then has to be supplied externally, and the controller reports an error if asked for it. A controller that cannot work at all without a simulation rejects the None actor itself — see ControllerMochiArticulatedPose, which drives Mochi’s built-in implicit PD controller.

The owning bot is inferred from robot (see get_bot_containing_actor()): if that actor is a bot’s articulation or one of its link actors, the controller is recorded against that bot, found by the bot-scoped finders, and destroyed with it; otherwise it has no owning bot. create_controller() is the more direct way to create one on a bot you already hold, and also carries an instance name.

Parameters:

  • type_name (str) – Registered controller type name.

  • prefab (Optional[BotPrefab]) – Optional borrowed robot-model description; may be None and must outlive the created controller.

  • robot (Optional[Actor]) – Articulated actor to control, or None for externally supplied observations.

  • name (str) – Instance name used by the name-based finders; need not be unique.

Returns:

Handle to the created controller, or an invalid handle on error.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

create_sensor(self: RoboticsContext, type_name: str, link_actor: superdex.physics.Actor, name: str = '', param_args: str = '') → SensorHandle

Create a sensor of the given type on the given link actor. paramArgs is an optional params file path or inline JSON string consumed by the factory; pass an empty view to use default-constructed parameters. name is the instance name used by find_sensors_by_name() and need not be unique. The owning bot is inferred from linkActor. Returns a handle. For bot-owned sensors, prefer declaring them in the BotPrefab so they are auto-instantiated and destroyed with the bot.

Parameters:

  • type_name (str) – Registered sensor type name.

  • link_actor (Optional[Actor]) – Actor to attach the sensor to, or None for an actor-less sensor.

  • name (str) – Instance name used by the name-based finders; need not be unique.

  • param_args (str) – Params file path or inline JSON; empty uses defaults.

Returns:

Handle to the created sensor, or an invalid handle on error.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Base class for robot sensors. Derives from ComponentBase for common lifecycle (validity, actor, destroy). Each derived sensor keeps its own specialized ComputeSignal signature.

get_parent_from_sensor(self: SensorBase) → superdex.physics.TransformRT

The sensor’s pose relative to its parent frame: the associated link’s actor for bot-owned sensors, or the scene root for scene-level / actor-less sensors. aFromB convention (maps sensor-frame coordinates into the parent frame).

Returns:

Sensor pose relative to its parent frame.

get_world_transform(self: SensorBase) → superdex.physics.TransformRT

The sensor’s pose in world space. When the sensor is bound to a Mochi Actor, that actor’s transform is already world-resolved by the simulation, so world = actorWorldTransform * parentFromSensor. When the sensor has no actor (a fusion sensor that consumes other sensors, or a scene sensor standing in for a scene root that has no Mochi actor), the scene root is the parent: world = parentFromSensor, i.e. the scene-root-to-world transform is treated as identity (a surrogate for a real scene-root actor) until scene spawn transforms are supported.

Returns:

Sensor pose in world space.

build_articulated_pose_from_bot_pose(bot_prefab: BotPrefab, src_pose: Span[SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex], num_actor_dofs: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex) → superdex.physics.DynamicArrayReal

Convert a bot-space pose to an articulated-actor pose.

Bot DOFs never include the root joint’s, whether or not the articulation has any: a Free root contributes 6 actor DOFs that bot space excludes, and a Hard root contributes none. The two spaces therefore share an order and differ only by that leading offset, so this copies srcPose to pose[i + numBaseDofs] and zero-fills the base DOFs, producing the actor-DOF layout set_articulated_pose_from_joints() expects. It never permutes.

Parameters:

  • bot_prefab (BotPrefab) – Bot describing the articulation.

  • src_pose (ArrayLikeReal) – Bot-space pose (must have superdex::robotics::BotPrefab::_numDofs entries).

  • num_actor_dofs (int) – The actor’s DOF count (get_num_dofs()).

Returns:

Pose in actor-DOF layout, sized to numActorDofs.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Warning

This documentation references the following C++ API, which is not available in Python: superdex::robotics::BotPrefab::_numDofs.

load_bot_prefab_from_urdf_file(path: str) → BotPrefab

Load bot parameters from a URDF file.

Parses the URDF and resolves each link’s visual and collision mesh references relative to the URDF location (ROS package:// URIs are supported), storing the resolved on-disk paths in the returned prefab. Collision meshes may be any format the shape loader accepts (e.g. .stl, .obj, .ply, .off, .mochi.h5); when a collision mesh carries no baked SDF, one is generated on demand at bot creation. A free world_joint is injected at index 0.

Parameters:

path (str) – Path to the .urdf file.

Returns:

The loaded or built BotPrefab.

Raises:

Error – If an error occurs.

Note

Only <mesh> geometry is imported. Primitive URDF shapes (<box>, <cylinder>, <sphere>) in <visual> / <collision> elements are not supported and are silently skipped; the importer uses the first mesh-bearing visual/collision on each link.

register_python_actuator(bots_ctx: RoboticsContext, type_name: str, factory: object) → None

Register an actuator type implemented in Python. factory is called with (actor, param_args) – the link Actor, which an actuator always has, and the actuator’s params (a file path or inline JSON, empty for defaults) – and must return a Python actuator instance, which must define reset() (an empty body is fine) – the framework invokes it between episodes. Retrieve the live instance to drive it with get_python_actuator.

register_python_controller(bots_ctx: RoboticsContext, type_name: str, factory: object) → None

Register a controller type implemented in Python. factory is called with the robot Actor (None if the controller was created without one) and must return a Python controller instance. The instance must define reset() (an empty body is fine); its optional configure_from_scene_entry(param_args, init_args) is also invoked by the framework. Retrieve the live instance to drive it with get_python_controller.

register_python_sensor(bots_ctx: RoboticsContext, type_name: str, factory: object) → None

Register a sensor type implemented in Python. factory is called with (actor, param_args) – the link Actor, or None for an actor-less sensor, and the sensor’s params (a file path or inline JSON, empty for defaults) – and must return a Python sensor instance, which must define reset() (an empty body is fine) – the framework invokes it between episodes. Retrieve the live instance to drive it with get_python_sensor.
